items.title: When you look under the hood, those U.S. job numbers in August weren’t that hot.
items.content:
When you look under the hood, those U.S. job numbers in August weren’t that hot.
 x.com/kurtsaltrichter/status… Kurt S. Altrichter, CRPS® (@kurtsaltrichter)The 162,000 jobs everyone cheered came from waiters, bartenders, and a soccer tournament.

Food services and drinking places added 59,000 in August, the biggest gain by far and nearly 5x the 12-month average. Temporary FIFA World Cup hiring did most of the lifting. Information, finance, and government all shed jobs.

The highest-paying sectors are shrinking while low-wage temporary work carries the headline. Strip out the World Cup and this labor market is cooling.—  https://x.com/kurtsaltrichter/status/2096274160125169742 
— Steve Hanke (@steve_hanke) Sep 6, 2026
